title_en: Song Yu v. Beijing Shenghefa Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Guangdong Yuecai Investment Holding Co., Ltd., and Beijing Urban and Rural Construction Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over pre-sale contract of commercial housing
ruling_gist_en: The buyer and the developer both claimed the existence of a real and valid commercial housing sale relationship between them, and relied on Article 2 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Priority of Compensation for Construction Project Price, which provides that 'after a consumer has paid all or most of the funds for the purchase of a commercial housing unit, the contractor's priority right to compensation for the construction project price with respect to that commercial housing shall not prevail against the buyer,' to oppose the contractor's claim for compensation for the construction project price. However, there were numerous doubts concerning the important facts such as the signing of the housing purchase contract and payment of the purchase price, and the statements of the parties on multiple occasions were inconsistent and contradictory. The basis for determining the existence of a real commercial housing sale relationship between the parties was clearly insufficient. Under such circumstances, the buyer's request for the developer to handle the house registration transfer in accordance with the commercial housing sale contract shall be dismissed.

full_text_en:
Song Yu v. Beijing Shenghefa Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Guangdong Yuecai Investment Holding Co., Ltd., and Beijing Urban and Rural Construction Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract

Ruling Summary

Where both the purchaser and the developer assert that a genuine and valid commercial housing sale relationship exists between the parties, and rely on Article 2 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Priority Right to Payment for Construction Project Costs, which provides that "after a consumer pays all or most of the purchase price for a commercial housing unit, the contractor's priority right to payment for the construction project costs for such commercial housing shall not prevail against the purchaser," to oppose the contractor's claim for payment for construction project costs, but there are numerous suspicious points with respect to the material facts such as the signing of the housing purchase contract and the payment of the purchase price, the statements of the parties are inconsistent and contradictory on multiple occasions, and the evidence based on which a genuine and valid commercial housing sale relationship between the parties is established is clearly insufficient. Under such circumstances, the purchaser's request for the developer to handle the registration of housing title transfer in accordance with the commercial housing sale contract shall be dismissed.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 331

Applicant for retrial (Plaintiff at first instance, Appellant at second instance, Applicant for retrial): Song Yu, male, Han ethnicity, born July 8, 1967, residing at No. 7, East District, Yard 14, Fuxing Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Liu Fei, attorney at Beijing Weiling Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance, Appellee at second instance, Respondent): Beijing Shenghefa Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 24 Shijia Hutong, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal representative: Yang Xiaonan, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhong Yuqing, attorney at Beijing Jinli Law Firm.

Respondent (Third party at first instance, Appellee at second instance, Respondent): Guangdong Yuecai Investment Holding Co., Ltd. (formerly Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd. Beijing Branch), domiciled at 15th Floor, Yuecai Building, No. 481 Dongfeng Zhong Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Liang Tang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xueming, attorney at Guangdong Sanliang Law Firm.

Respondent (Third party at first instance, Appellee at second instance, Respondent): Beijing Urban and Rural Construction Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 7, Yard 8, Caoqiao East Road, Fengtai District, Beijing.

Legal representative: Liu Chongze, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jing Baohua, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xinhua, attorney at Beijing Zhongyun Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Song Yu, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2010) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1715 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case concerning a dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract with the respondents Beijing Shenghefa Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Shenghefa Company), Guangdong Yuecai Investment Holding Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Yuecai Company), and Beijing Urban and Rural Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Urban and Rural Construction), applied to this Court for retrial. On August 24, 2011, this Court rendered the civil ruling (2011) Min Jian Zi No. 369, deciding to retry this case and suspend the enforcement of the original judgment. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on November 11, 2011. Liu Fei, the agent ad litem of Song Yu, Zhong Yuqing, the agent ad litem of Shenghefa Company, Zhang Xueming, the agent ad litem of Yuecai Company, and Jing Baohua and Chen Xinhua, the agents ad litem of Urban and Rural Construction, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter Beijing Second Intermediate Court) found at first instance: Shenghe Jiayuan is a project invested and constructed by Shenghefa Company, comprising two 24-story residential buildings and one ancillary building. On September 7, 1999, Shenghefa Company obtained the construction land planning permit for the Shenghe Jiayuan project. In March 2000, Shenghefa Company obtained the construction project commencement certificate. In September 2000, Shenghefa Company obtained the state-owned land use certificate. In December 2002, Shenghefa Company obtained the pre-sale permit for Buildings 1-3 of Shenghe Jiayuan. The project underwent completion acceptance on April 26, 2002. In July 2006, Shenghefa Company obtained the general property ownership certificate for the project.

On April 25, 2001, Song Yu and Shenghefa Company executed 17 commercial housing sale contracts numbered No. 125415, No. 125418, No. 125416, No. 125417, No. 125419, No. 125420, No. 125421, No. 125422, No. 125423, No. 125424, No. 125425, No. 130131, No. 130132, No. 130133, No. 130134, No. 130135, and No. 130136. The above 17 contracts stipulated that Song Yu would purchase from Shenghefa Company the following units in Building 2, Shenghe Jiayuan, Yard 2, Anhui Dongli, Chaoyang District, Beijing: 23-A2, 7-C2, 20-D1, 6-C2, 8-C2, 14-B2, 15-B2, 16-B2, 18-B2, 19-B2, 21-B2, 3-A1, 3-B1, 3-D2, 2-D1, 4-C2, and 17-C2. The unit price for each of the 17 units was RMB 5,082 per square meter, and the total price was RMB 10,190,728. Article 15 of each of the above 17 contracts provided: "The seller shall, within 360 days after the delivery of the commercial housing for use, file with the real estate registration authority the documents required to be provided by the seller for the registration of title. If, due to the seller's responsibility, the buyer is unable to obtain the real estate title certificate within the prescribed period, the parties agree to handle the matter in accordance with items (1) and (2) below: (1) The buyer withdraws from the purchase, and the seller shall refund to the buyer the purchase price paid within 30 days from the date the buyer requests withdrawal, and compensate the buyer for losses at 1% of the purchase price paid; (2) The buyer does not withdraw from the purchase, and the seller shall pay to the buyer liquidated damages at 1% of the purchase price paid."

After the contracts were signed, Song Yu paid the full purchase price to Shenghefa Company during the period from April 26, 2001 to April 28, 2002. Shenghefa Company acknowledged receipt of the full purchase price and issued payment receipts to Song Yu. Shenghefa Company did not apply for contract registration and filing with the real estate administration department as agreed in the contracts. On May 28, 2003, Shenghefa Company issued a housing occupancy notice to Song Yu, notifying Song Yu to go to the Shenghe Jiayuan property management company to handle the check-in procedures. Song Yu acknowledged that he actually took possession of all the units on May 28, 2003.

It was additionally found that on July 12, 2001, in order to apply for a loan from Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd. Beijing Branch (hereinafter Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch), Shenghefa Company mortgaged 129 units under construction, including the 17 units in dispute, in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan to Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, and completed the mortgage registration with the real estate administration department. The scope of the mortgage right was RMB 40,000,000. Because Shenghefa Company was unable to repay the loan on time, on July 10, 2003, Shenghefa Company and Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch entered into another loan contract, borrowing RMB 18,680,000 to repay the previous loan. The term of this loan was from September 18, 2003 to April 17, 2004. Shenghefa Company mortgaged 71 units it owned in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, including the 17 units in dispute, as security. On the same day, the parties signed a mortgage contract. On September 15, 2003, the above units completed the mortgage registration procedures with the real estate administration department.

In March 2004, Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch filed a civil lawsuit with the Beijing Second Intermediate Court, requesting that Shenghefa Company repay the remaining loan ahead of schedule, pay interest, compound interest, and related expenses, and that it be entitled to priority compensation from the mortgaged properties. On June 2, 2004, the Beijing Second Intermediate Court rendered the civil judgment (2004) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 04276 in the case of Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch v. Shenghefa Company, confirming that the loan contract and mortgage contract between Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch and Shenghefa Company were valid, ordering Shenghefa Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 17,480,000, interest, compound interest, and attorney fees to Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, and confirming that Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch was entitled to priority compensation from the properties mortgaged by Shenghefa Company (including the 17 units in dispute). This judgment has become legally effective.

It was further found that on November 5, 2004, the Beijing Arbitration Commission ruled that Shenghefa Company should deliver one of the units in dispute, Unit 15-B2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, to the Beijing Junxiao Science and Technology Development Institute (hereinafter Junxiao Institute), complete the commercial housing sale contract registration and filing procedures for Junxiao Institute, and assist Junxiao Institute in obtaining the housing ownership certificate. After being given clarification, Song Yu still insisted on continuing to perform the commercial housing sale contract he signed with Shenghefa Company for the purchase of Unit 15-B2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, and insisted on requesting Shenghefa Company to handle the housing ownership certificate for that unit.

It was additionally found that Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch raised objections to the authenticity of the commercial housing sale contracts signed between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company, and adduced the following evidence to support its assertion: (1) A key handover letter stamped by Shenghefa Company on April 29, 2002, and a sales summary table for Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan. This table showed that the 17 units purchased by Song Yu were not listed among the units already sold; (2) An IOU and detail list stamped by Shenghefa Company on May 22, 2002. This IOU and appendix still showed that the 17 units purchased by Song Yu were not sold; (3) In 2003, when Shenghefa Company again mortgaged the disputed units to Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, it did not declare that the disputed units had already been sold to Song Yu; (4) An audit report prepared in October 2001 by Beijing New Generation Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter New Generation Firm) commissioned by Shenghefa Company. This audit report showed that on May 8, 2001, Shenghefa Company entered into a loan contract with Huanan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Huanan Industrial), borrowing RMB 11,000,000 with a term of one month. Shenghefa Company repaid the loan to Huanan Industrial on July 25, 2001. In the company's accounts and accounting vouchers, this RMB 11,000,000 was recorded as a loan from Song Yu and had been repaid. Therefore, the relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company was a loan relationship, not a housing sale relationship.

Song Yu alleged at first instance: In 2001, he signed 17 commercial housing sale contracts with Shenghefa Company to purchase 17 units in Shenghe Jiayuan, Yard 2, Anhui Dongli, Chaoyang District, Beijing, developed by Shenghefa Company. From April 26, 2001 to April 28, 2002, he paid a total of RMB 10,190,728 to Shenghefa Company as the full purchase price. On May 28, 2003, Shenghefa Company handled the check-in procedures for him, but to date, Shenghefa Company has still not handled the property ownership certificates in accordance with the contract. Therefore, he filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting: 1. Confirmation that the 17 commercial housing sale contracts are lawful and valid; 2. An order that Shenghefa Company pay liquidated damages of RMB 101,907.28 for delayed title certificate handling and economic losses of RMB 5,898,092.72; 3. An order that Shenghefa Company handle the property ownership certificates for the corresponding units; 4. An order that Shenghefa Company bear the litigation costs of this case.

Shenghefa Company argued in defense: It agreed with Song Yu's first and third requests; it agreed to pay Song Yu the liquidated damages for delayed title certificate handling as stipulated in the contract; it disagreed with compensating for losses, as the delay in handling the title certificate did not cause other losses to Song Yu.

Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch stated: In order to obtain a loan from Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, Shenghefa Company had mortgaged all the units in dispute to Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, and had completed the mortgage registration with the real estate administration department. The effective judgment of the Beijing Second Intermediate Court had already confirmed that it was entitled to priority compensation from the mortgaged properties, including the units in dispute. Moreover, Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch had sufficient evidence to prove that the commercial housing sale contracts signed between Shenghefa Company and Song Yu were fraudulent. Therefore, Song Yu was not entitled to obtain ownership of the units in dispute.

The Beijing Second Intermediate Court held at first instance: Both Song Yu and Shenghefa Company acknowledged that the 17 commercial housing sale contracts signed on April 25, 2001 were voluntarily executed by the parties, and the above 17 commercial housing sale contracts did not contain any provisions that violated mandatory or prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, it should be determined that the 17 commercial housing sale contracts represented the true intentions of the parties and were lawful and valid. Although Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch adduced evidence to prove that Shenghefa Company had once denied the sale of the disputed units and that there was a loan relationship between Shenghefa Company and Song Yu, the above evidence was insufficient to negate the authenticity of the 17 commercial housing sale contracts signed between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company. Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch's claim in this regard lacked sufficient evidence and was not supported.

Shenghefa Company acknowledged that Song Yu had paid the full purchase price in accordance with the contract, so Song Yu had fully performed his contractual obligations, and Shenghefa Company should also assist Song Yu in handling the housing ownership certificates for the purchased units within the period stipulated in the contract. Song Yu now filed a lawsuit requesting Shenghefa Company to handle the housing ownership certificates for the units in dispute, and Shenghefa Company also agreed with Song Yu's claim. Therefore, Song Yu's request in this regard should be supported. However, the effective arbitration award had already confirmed that Shenghefa Company should deliver Unit 15-B2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, one of the units in dispute, to Junxiao Institute, and assist Junxiao Institute in handling the housing ownership certificate. In that case, the commercial housing sale contract between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company for the purchase of Unit 15-B2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan could no longer be performed. Given that Song Yu, after being given clarification, still insisted on his claim, his request for Shenghefa Company to handle the housing ownership certificate for Unit 15-B2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan was dismissed.

Furthermore, Song Yu, based on the commercial housing sale contracts he signed with Shenghefa Company, requested Shenghefa Company to handle the housing ownership certificates for the units in dispute. He only held a creditor's right with respect to the units in dispute. The effective judgment had already confirmed that Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch was entitled to priority compensation from the properties mortgaged by Shenghefa Company (including the 17 units in dispute), and this priority right originated from the mortgage right. Therefore, if Shenghefa Company failed to repay the debt to Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch in a timely manner, the mortgagee, Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch, could seek satisfaction from the mortgaged property by discounting or by receiving priority payment over ordinary creditors from the proceeds of the mortgaged property. Only after the mortgagee exercised its mortgage right could Shenghefa Company perform the commercial housing sale contracts signed with Song Yu and handle the housing ownership certificates for the purchased units. Therefore, only after the priority right of Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch over the mortgaged property was fully realized could Shenghefa Company handle the housing ownership certificates for the remaining units for Song Yu.

Shenghefa Company failed to handle the housing ownership certificates for the units in dispute for Song Yu within the period stipulated in the contracts, thereby breaching the provisions of Article 15 of the contracts and should bear liability for breach of contract. Regarding the amount of liquidated damages for delayed title certificate handling, Article 15 of the commercial housing sale contracts contained a clear stipulation, and Shenghefa Company also agreed to pay in accordance with the contract. Song Yu's claim for liquidated damages for delayed title certificate handling based on Article 15 of the contract had sufficient contractual basis and should be supported. Song Yu claimed that Shenghefa Company's delay in handling the title certificate caused him losses beyond the liquidated damages, but he did not adduce evidence to prove such losses, and this claim was not supported. In summary, the judgment (2006) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 16218 was rendered: 1. The commercial housing sale contracts numbered No. 125415, No. 125418, No. 125416, No. 125417, No. 125419, No. 125420, No. 125421, No. 125422, No. 125423, No. 125424, No. 125425, No. 130131, No. 130132, No. 130133, No. 130134, No. 130135, and No. 130136 between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company were valid; 2. Within 30 days after the realization of Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch's priority right over the units in dispute, Shenghefa Company shall handle for Song Yu the housing ownership certificates for the units under the contracts specified in paragraph 1 of the judgment, except for the units discounted, auctioned, or sold due to the exercise of Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch's priority right and Unit 15-B2 under commercial housing sale contract No. 125421; 3. Shenghefa Company shall pay to Song Yu liquidated damages of RMB 101,907.28 for delayed title certificate handling within seven days after this judgment takes effect; 4. Dismissed all other claims of Song Yu; 5. Dismissed all other claims of Guangfa Bank Beijing Branch. The case acceptance fee was RMB 40,010, to be borne by Song Yu in the amount of RMB 39,310 and by Shenghefa Company in the amount of RMB 700.

After the above judgment took effect, Urban and Rural Construction, asserting that the judgment infringed upon its lawful rights and interests, applied to the Beijing High People's Court (hereinafter Beijing High Court) for retrial. On December 26, 2008, the Beijing High Court rendered the civil ruling (2008) Gao Min Shen Zi No. 3230, ordering the Beijing Second Intermediate Court to retry this case.

During the retrial at the Beijing Second Intermediate Court, Urban and Rural Construction applied to participate in the proceedings as a third party, and the court granted permission in accordance with the law. Song Yu stated that his purchase of housing was not a conventional housing purchase; the evidence provided by the third party was all circumstantial evidence and insufficient to prove that the commercial housing sale contracts signed between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company were false and invalid. He maintained his original opinion. The original judgment was correct, and he requested that the retrial uphold it. Yuecai Company stated that it maintained its original opinion; it was entitled to priority compensation for the disputed units pursuant to the effective judgment, and the commercial housing sale contracts signed between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company were fraudulent contracts. Urban and Rural Construction argued that Song Yu and Shenghefa Company acted in malicious collusion, and the commercial housing sale contracts they signed were fraudulent and void contracts, requesting that the retrial amend the judgment according to law.

During the retrial, the Beijing Second Intermediate Court confirmed the additional findings and further findings of fact from the original trial. It also found that Shenghe Jiayuan is a project invested and constructed by Shenghefa Company, comprising two 24-story residential buildings and one ancillary building. On September 7, 1999, Shenghefa Company obtained the construction land planning permit for the Shenghe Jiayuan project. In March 2000, Shenghefa Company obtained the construction project commencement certificate. In September 2000, Shenghefa Company obtained the state-owned land use certificate. On April 26, 2002, the Shenghe Jiayuan project underwent completion acceptance, and in May of the same year, check-in procedures began. In December 2002, Shenghefa Company obtained the pre-sale permit for Buildings 1-3 of Shenghe Jiayuan. In July 2006, Shenghefa Company obtained the general property ownership certificate for the Shenghe Jiayuan project.

During the retrial, Song Yu claimed that in April 2001, Wang Yongwei, then the legal representative of Shenghefa Company, borrowed RMB 11 million from him. On May 8, 2004, Song Yu and Shenghefa Company entered into two loan contracts with loan amounts of RMB 10 million and RMB 1 million, respectively. Subsequently, Wang Yongwei indicated that the Shenghe Jiayuan houses would be sold to Song Yu at a relatively low price to offset the loan. Song Yu then signed 37 commercial housing sales contracts with Shenghefa Company in his own name and in the names of third parties Zhang Jingsheng and Guan Hongbiao, with the contract signing date written as April 25, 2001. After the contracts were signed, Song Yu claimed that he paid the remaining purchase price from April 2001 to 2002 through bank transfers and cash, until all purchase price of RMB 23,776,740 was paid on April 28, 2002, and stated that Shenghefa Company had delayed and refused to issue purchase invoices, instead issuing receipts, and replaced them with new receipts after the legal representative of Shenghefa Company was changed to Yang Xiaonan. Regarding the loan contract and repayment vouchers between Shenghefa Company and Huanan Industry on May 8, 2001, during the original trial, Song Yu stated that at the end of June 2001, because he wanted to cancel the purchase and demand a refund, Shenghefa Company indicated that it could first refund RMB 11 million, but required the signing of a loan contract to facilitate financial accounting. Accordingly, Song Yu signed a loan contract in the name of Huanan Industry, refunded RMB 11 million, and then later wanted to continue purchasing the houses, so he returned the RMB 11 million in cash to Shenghefa Company. During the retrial, Song Yu stated that in July 2001, Wang Yongwei asked Song Yu to help with account processing, so he signed a loan contract for RMB 11 million in the name of Huanan Industry. Wang Yongwei paid Huanan Industry by check, and later withdrew the RMB 11 million in cash. Urban and Rural Construction argued that Song Yu's statements regarding the purchase process contained multiple contradictions and that the purchase was fraudulent. It applied to the court to obtain from the public security bureau file the following evidence: a certificate from the Housing Transaction Market Management Office of Beijing Municipal Construction Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Housing Management Office of the Municipal Construction Committee), a certificate from Beijing Wuyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., a certificate from Beijing Jingjin Color Printing Co., Ltd., the interview record of Jiang Lei (employee of Beijing Wanquan Garden Property Development Co., Ltd.), the loan contract between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company, the interview record of Song Yu, the interview record of Wang Baosong, the interview record of Wang Bing, the interview record of Liu Qian, the interview record of Zong Qiuxiang, the accounting statements of Shenghefa Company, the audit report, and the sales control table of Shenghefa Company. Yuecai Company agreed with the opinion of Urban and Rural Construction.

Upon investigation, prior to March 15, 2005, the commercial housing sales contract forms used by real estate development enterprises for pre-sale commercial housing were obtained from the Housing Management Office of the Municipal Construction Committee or directly from the printing factory. Blank contracts numbered 125401 to 125425 were collected by Beijing Wuyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and blank contracts numbered 130126 to 130150 were collected by Beijing Wanquan Garden Property Development Co., Ltd. The disputed contract texts numbered 125415, 125417–125423, 125425, 130131–130135, among others, had already been signed and used by the above two companies.

Wang Bing, former cashier of Shenghefa Company, stated in the interview record of the public security bureau that during her tenure from October 1999 to November 2001, Wang Yongwei, the then legal representative of Shenghefa Company, instructed her, together with Liu Qian and Liang Aijun, to collect from Song Yu a check, cash, and bank card for a loan of RMB 11 million around the end of April 2001, which was repaid by check in July 2001. She also stated that during her tenure, she had not heard of Song Yu, Zhang Jingsheng, or Guan Hongbiao purchasing houses, nor had the company received large amounts of purchase price. In financial procedures for house sales, receipts were issued for the deposit, and invoices were issued upon payment of the down payment. She stated that the receipts for the purchase price provided by Song Yu for 2001 were not issued by her, and she was not aware of the specific circumstances.

Liu Qian, former accountant of Shenghefa Company, stated in the interview record of the public security bureau that during her tenure from May 2000 to November 2001, Wang Yongwei, the then legal representative of Shenghefa Company, instructed her, together with Wang Bing and Liang Aijun, to collect from Song Yu a check, cash, and bank card for a loan of RMB 11 million (the specific date was unclear), which was repaid by check in July 2001. She also stated that during her tenure, Song Yu had not purchased any houses. In financial procedures for house sales, only deposit receipts were issued, and invoices were issued for the purchase price. She stated that she had never seen the receipts for the purchase price provided by Song Yu for 2001.

Zong Qiuxiang, former deputy general manager of Shenghefa Company, stated in the interview record of the public security bureau that during his tenure from 2000 to November 2001, he was responsible for supervising the sale of the Shenghe Jiayuan houses. He had never seen Song Yu, Zhang Jingsheng, or Guan Hongbiao purchase any houses, but he had heard Wang Yongwei, the then legal representative of Shenghefa Company, mention borrowing RMB 11 million from Song Yu.

Wang Baosong, former deputy general manager of Shenghefa Company, stated in the interview record of the public security bureau that after he joined the company in early 2002, he heard from Yang Xiaonan, the then legal representative of Shenghefa Company, that Song Yu, Zhang Jingsheng, and Guan Hongbiao had purchased 37 houses from the former legal representative Wang Yongwei, paying a total of approximately RMB 23 million, all of which were issued with receipts. He also stated that during Yang Xiaonan's tenure, he handled the issuance of receipts, and the receipts issued during Wang Yongwei's tenure were retrieved and replaced with new receipts. At the same time, Wang Baosong stated that he was unaware of the circumstances of the contract signing and payment during Wang Yongwei's tenure.

Another investigation found that evidence materials such as the key transfer letter issued by Shenghefa Company with its seal on April 29, 2002, the sales summary table for Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, the IOU and detailed list issued by Shenghefa Company with its seal on May 22, 2002, and the sales control table of Shenghefa Company all indicated that the disputed 37 houses (including the 17 houses purchased in Song Yu's name) were not sold and were not included in the sold houses.

Another investigation found that in the accounting statements of Shenghefa Company from January to September 2001, the entry for the subject name Song Yu in the occurrence and balance table recorded a debit of RMB 11 million and a credit of RMB 11 million for the current period. In November 2001, the audit report commissioned by Shenghefa Company from New Generation Accounting Firm showed that on May 8, 2001, Shenghefa Company entered into a loan contract with Huanan Industry, borrowing RMB 11 million for a period of one month. On July 25, 2001, Shenghefa Company repaid the RMB 11 million loan to Huanan Industry. In the detailed list of funding sources and the detailed list of current accounts for the Shenghe Jiayuan project, this RMB 11 million was recorded as a loan from Song Yu and was recorded as having been repaid.

Another investigation found that after the disputed commercial housing sales contracts were signed, the parties did not apply to the real estate management department for contract registration and filing as agreed. Song Yu stated that on May 28, 2003, Shenghefa Company issued a move-in notice (the date on the notice was blank), and he completed the move-in procedures on that day but did not actually move in, nor did he sign a property management contract.

Further investigation found that on March 13, 2000, Urban and Rural Construction and Shenghefa Company entered into a Beijing construction project construction contract, stipulating that Urban and Rural Construction would construct the commercial residential and supporting public buildings for Buildings 1 to 3 of Shenghe Jiayuan, with a total contract price of RMB 112,842,092. The project commenced on March 27, 2000, and was completed and delivered for use after passing the completion acceptance as agreed on April 26, 2002. On August 8, 2003, Urban and Rural Construction and Shenghefa Company entered into a supplementary agreement on project settlement, determining the final total settlement price of the project to be RMB 116,000,000. Apart from the RMB 68,106,400 already paid, Shenghefa Company still owed RMB 47,393,600. After the above agreement was signed, Shenghefa Company paid Urban and Rural Construction RMB 500,000 on October 14 and 17, 2003, but did not pay the remaining amount, including liquidated damages. Subsequently, Urban and Rural Construction filed two lawsuits with Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, requesting that Shenghefa Company be ordered to pay the project payment and corresponding liquidated damages, and that Urban and Rural Construction be confirmed to have priority compensation rights over the completed project. Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court issued civil judgments on July 1, 2004, in Cases (2004) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 623 and (2004) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 4023, ordering Shenghefa Company to pay Urban and Rural Construction a total of RMB 47,393,600 for the project and corresponding liquidated damages, and dismissing Urban and Rural Construction's claims for confirmation of priority compensation rights over the completed project. These judgments have become legally effective.

Furthermore, based on the non-performing asset transfer agreement signed between Guangdong Development Bank Co., Ltd. and Yuecai Company on December 31, 2005, the Beijing Branch of Guangdong Development Bank entered into a single loan creditor's rights transfer agreement with Yuecai Company on October 31, 2006, transferring to Yuecai Company the creditor's rights and all rights arising from the loan contract between the Beijing Branch of Guangdong Development Bank and Shenghefa Company. Subsequently, on November 20, 2006, the notice of creditor's rights transfer and demand for payment, notice of transfer of guarantee rights and demand, and notice of repayment account were served on Shenghefa Company, and the service was notarized. On June 27, 2007, the Beijing Branch of Guangdong Development Bank published a notice of creditor's rights transfer and demand in the People's Court Daily.

Additionally, on October 20, 2008, Shenghefa Company was lawfully revoked and its enterprise legal person business license was canceled.

Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held in the retrial that when exercising rights and performing obligations, the parties shall adhere to the principle of good faith. In this case, although Song Yu provided the commercial housing sales contract, receipts for the purchase price, and move-in notice signed with Shenghefa Company in support of his claims, his statements on important facts such as contract signing, payment of the purchase price, and loans were inconsistent between the original trial and the retrial. In light of the relevant evidence collected by the court from the public security bureau file and the sales records of Shenghefa Company, it was shown that Song Yu did not actually purchase the disputed houses, and the disputed houses were not sold. Therefore, the existing evidence was insufficient to prove the existence of a commercial housing sale relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company. Song Yu's request to confirm the validity of the commercial housing sales contract between the parties and other corresponding claims were not supported. Since there was already an effective judgment confirming that Yuecai Company had priority compensation rights over the mortgaged properties of Shenghefa Company (including the disputed houses), no further repetition was necessary. In summary, the court issued Civil Judgment (2009) Er Zhong Min Zai Chu Zi No. 17337: 1. Revoking Civil Judgment (2006) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 16218; 2. Dismissing Song Yu's claims; 3. Dismissing Yuecai Company's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 40,010 was borne by Song Yu.

Song Yu, dissatisfied with this judgment, appealed to Beijing High People's Court, arguing that he had repeatedly submitted evidence such as the commercial housing sales contract, receipts for the purchase price, and move-in notice, which together formed a complete chain of evidence sufficient to prove that he had actually obtained ownership of the houses. The first instance judgment, by using evidence of lower probative value to override evidence of higher probative value, reached a wrong conclusion and should be reversed. He requested the court to find the facts, render a judgment revoking the first instance judgment, maintaining Civil Judgment (2006) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 16218, and ordering Urban and Rural Construction to bear the litigation costs. Shenghefa Company argued that it agreed with Song Yu's appeal requests. Yuecai Company argued that Yuecai Company had priority compensation rights, and agreed with the opinion of Urban and Rural Construction on the facts. The first instance judgment was correct, and the court of second instance was requested to dismiss the appeal and uphold the first instance judgment. Urban and Rural Construction argued that the commercial housing sales contract in this case was fraudulent, and the 17 disputed contract texts were forged. The contract signing date and purchase receipts were false. Song Yu did not actually pay the purchase price and did not actually move in. A review of the case file showed that Song Yu had not purchased the disputed houses at all. The probative value of the witness testimony relied upon by Urban and Rural Construction was far higher than the documentary evidence provided by Song Yu. In summary, it requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first instance judgment be affirmed.

In the second instance, Beijing High People's Court found that the facts were consistent with those found in the first instance, except that during the trial, Song Yu stated the following regarding the payment: The occurrence of RMB 11 million was based on a loan, and only later did the loan contracts between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company come into existence. Song Yu and the legal representative of Shenghefa Company were friends, and the loan was based on mutual trust. Before April 30, 2001, Song Yu lent RMB 11 million to Shenghefa Company by check, cash, and bank card. On May 8, 2001, Song Yu and Shenghefa Company signed two loan contracts, one for RMB 10 million and one for RMB 1 million. Song Yu signed the contracts that day but left them with Shenghefa Company, which did not sign or seal them at that time. The signing should have occurred later, and these details only came to Song Yu's mind later. In May 2001, Song Yu lent another RMB 4.5 million to Shenghefa Company by bank card and cash, but no contract was signed. From mid-June to July 2001, Shenghefa Company told Song Yu that it was unable to repay the RMB 15.5 million loan and hoped Song Yu would purchase the company's houses, converting the loan into a purchase price. After negotiations, Song Yu agreed to purchase 37 properties in his own name and in the names of Zhang Jingsheng and Guan Hongbiao at a price of RMB 5,082 per square meter, slightly below market price, with the loan amount offsetting 65% of the purchase price. At the end of June 2001, the commercial housing sales contracts were signed, with the date backdated to April 25, 2001. Since the houses were not yet built at the time, the parties agreed that the remaining purchase price would be paid after the houses were completed. On July 15, 2001, Wang Yongwei and Yang Xiaonan asked Song Yu to assist with obtaining cash, so a loan contract was signed, and Shenghefa Company issued a check for RMB 10.5 million to Huanan Industry in the name of repayment. After the check proceeds reached Huanan Industry's account, Song Yu personally returned RMB 10.5 million in cash to Shenghefa Company in two payments: one of RMB 5 million and one of RMB 5.5 million. The contract between Huanan Industry and Shenghefa Company was signed on May 8, 2001, for an amount of RMB 11 million. On July 25, 2001, Huanan Industry issued a receipt to Shenghefa Company for RMB 10.5 million, stated as an intercompany transaction for account transfer purposes. In 2002, Song Yu successively paid over RMB 8 million in purchase price to Shenghefa Company, including RMB 6.5 million by check.

Furthermore, the 17 commercial housing sales contracts that Song Yu claimed to have signed with Shenghefa Company were numbered No. 125415, No. 125418, No. 125416, No. 125417, No. 125419, No. 125420, No. 125421, No. 125422, No. 125423, No. 125424, No. 125425, No. 130131, No. 130132, No. 130133, No. 130134, No. 130135, and No. 130136. These corresponded to houses located in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan at No. 2 Yard, Anhuidongli, Chaoyang District, Beijing: Units 23-A2, 7-C2, 20-D1, 6-C2, 8-C2, 14-B2, 15-B2, 16-B2, 18-B2, 19-B2, 21-B2, 3-A1, 3-B1, 3-D2, 2-D1, 4-C2, and 17-C2. The unit price for these 17 houses was RMB 5,082 per square meter, with a total price of RMB 10,190,728.

Beijing High People's Court held in the second instance that when exercising rights and performing obligations, the parties shall adhere to the principle of good faith. In this case, although Song Yu provided evidence such as the commercial housing sales contract executed with Shenghefa Company, receipts for the purchase price, and the move-in notice in support of his claims, his statements on important facts such as contract signing, payment of the purchase price, and loans were inconsistent. In light of the relevant evidence collected by the court from the public security bureau file and the sales records of Shenghefa Company, it was shown that the disputed houses were not sold. Therefore, the existing evidence was insufficient to prove the existence of a genuine and effective commercial housing sale relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company. Song Yu's request to confirm the validity of the commercial housing sales contract between the parties and other corresponding claims were not supported. In summary, the court issued Civil Judgment (2009) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 5744: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 40,010 was borne by Song Yu, and the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 2,338 was borne by Song Yu.

Song Yu, dissatisfied with the second instance judgment of Beijing High People's Court, applied to this court for retrial, arguing that: (1) He had repeatedly submitted evidence such as the commercial housing sales contract, receipts for the purchase price, and move-in notice, which together formed a complete chain of evidence sufficient to prove that he had actually obtained ownership of the houses. (2) The amount of repayment determined in the retrial judgment differed greatly from the amount of repayment stipulated in the relevant loan agreements, and the retrial judgment could not clarify whether the RMB 11 million loan had been repaid. (3) The confirmation action concerning the commercial housing pre-sale contract between him and Shenghefa Company was unrelated to Urban and Rural Construction, which was not a proper party in this case, and the original retrial procedure was unlawful. Therefore, he requested that the retrial judgment be revoked, the original judgment be affirmed, and Urban and Rural Construction bear the litigation costs.

On June 28, 2010, this court issued Civil Ruling (2010) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 64, instructing Beijing High People's Court to conduct a retrial.

In the retrial of Beijing High People's Court, it was found that during the retrial, Urban and Rural Construction provided the following new evidence: On February 28, 2005, May 20, 2005, and August 7, 2007, Ma Yanyun, Li Yiying, and Zhang Changqing respectively signed purchase contracts and obtained invoices with Shenghefa Company for the purchase of houses: Units 15-C1, 23-D2, and 3-D2 in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan. One of the sold houses, Unit 3-D2 of Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan, was included in the disputed properties in this case.

Furthermore, according to the investigation by the Enforcement Division of Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, most of the currently seized properties of Shenghefa Company had new rights holders and had already been occupied.

The other facts found in the retrial were consistent with those found in the second instance.

Beijing High People's Court held in the retrial that when exercising rights and performing obligations, the parties shall adhere to the principle of good faith. Although Song Yu provided evidence such as the commercial housing sales contract executed with Shenghefa Company, receipts for the purchase price, and the move-in notice in support of his claims, his statements on important facts such as contract signing, payment of the purchase price, and the performance of the loan contract with Shenghefa Company were contradictory. His statements involved a large amount of cash payments without other corroborating evidence and were contrary to common sense. The houses purchased by Song Yu were not recorded in the housing authority's filing system, and Song Yu did not provide formal purchase invoices. The sales records of Shenghefa Company, the key transfer documents, and the relevant testimony of Shenghefa Company's employees all showed that the houses purchased by Song Yu were not sold. The retrial found that Shenghefa Company had sold the disputed properties to others from 2005 onwards, which further confirmed that there was no genuine and effective commercial housing sale relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company. Song Yu's request to confirm the validity of the commercial housing sales contract and other corresponding claims were not supported. In summary, the court issued Civil Judgment (2010) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1715: affirming Civil Judgment (2009) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 5744.

Song Yu, still dissatisfied with the retrial judgment of the Beijing High People's Court, again filed a petition with this Court, alleging that: (1) The original retrial had procedural errors. Urban and Rural Construction was not a third party at first instance and did not meet the statutory requirements to be a third party in this case. The disputed house itself had nothing to do with Urban and Rural Construction, which had neither an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties nor any legal interest. Urban and Rural Construction, as a creditor of Shenghefa Company, was the subject of other litigation, not the subject of this case, and it did not meet the legal requirements for a third party. Adding it as a third party had no legal basis. The original trial illegally and erroneously established a third party and allowed it to initiate the retrial, which was the most fundamental procedural error. (2) The retrial judgment of the Beijing High People's Court found facts erroneously. The conversion of the original loan into a house purchase payment based on mutual agreement between him and Shenghefa Company did not violate relevant legal provisions; the house purchase was genuine, payment was actually made, the contract was legal and valid, and the evidence was complete and sufficient. The basic evidence in the retrial judgment, the "Record of Inquiry by the Fengtai Public Security Bureau," lacked authenticity, legality, and relevance, was illegal evidence, and had no evidentiary effect. The retrial judgment failed to recognize the fact that Song Yu had paid the remaining over 8 million yuan and evidence such as payment receipts and the occupancy notice, which had been verified during the court investigation, and instead inferred facts based on conjecture, showing an obvious bias. In summary, he requested the revocation of the Beijing High People's Court (2010) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1715 civil judgment and the affirmation of the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court (2006) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 16218 civil judgment.

Shenghefa Company argued in defense that it agreed with Song Yu's petition claims, and that the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court had no basis to list Urban and Rural Construction as a third party.

Yuecai Company argued in defense that Song Yu's petition claims were untenable, that this case had been tried multiple times, and that there was indeed a possibility of false collusion between Shenghefa Company and Song Yu. The retrial judgment of the Beijing High People's Court was correct and should be affirmed. Yuecai Company had a priority right to be compensated from the house involved in the case.

Urban and Rural Construction argued in defense that: (1) Urban and Rural Construction was a proper party in this case. The disputed property was the liable asset of Shenghefa Company for satisfying its construction project debt, so Urban and Rural Construction had a legal interest in this case and was fully qualified to participate in the litigation as a third party. (2) The commercial housing sales contract, payment receipt, and occupancy notice provided by Song Yu were all false; the commercial housing sales contract relationship between Song Yu and others and Shenghefa Company was entirely fictitious. From the flow of funds between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company, there was no genuine house purchase payment relationship. The records of inquiries with relevant personnel obtained by the Beijing High People's Court from the public security authorities also corroborated that there was no genuine house purchase relationship between the parties. Song Yu's statements regarding the timing of the house purchase, payment amounts, etc., were contradictory, some even diametrically opposite. In summary, the retrial judgment of the Beijing High People's Court had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures, and should be affirmed.

This Court finds upon retrial: According to the consistent acknowledgment of Song Yu and Shenghefa Company, the total price for the 37 houses purchased by Song Yu (17 purchased in Song Yu's name, 10 purchased in Zhang Jingsheng's name, and 10 purchased in Guan Hongbiao's name) was RMB 23,776,740. Among this, the cash portion totaled RMB 7,276,503.61, and the portion transferred by other entities or individuals totaled RMB 16,500,236.39. The specific transfer amounts are: Beijing Yongxin Spray Cotton Co., Ltd. RMB 996,685.47 (payment date: April 30, 2001); Beijing Dongcheng District Zhuyuan Food Store RMB 2,236,000 (payment date: April 30, 2001); Beijing Juyixin Commercial and Trading Co., Ltd. RMB 3,764,000 (payment date: April 30, 2001); Wang Bing RMB 1,000,000; Beijing Hongshiyuan Commercial and Trading Co., Ltd. RMB 2,000,000 (payment date: May 9, 2001); Beijing Ruilongsen Logistics Co., Ltd. RMB 1,303,550.92 (payment date: March 19, 2002); Beijing Fuhaihua Import and Export Co., Ltd. RMB 2,200,000 (payment date: March 25, 2002); Beijing Ruilongsen Logistics Co., Ltd. RMB 3,000,000 (payment date: April 28, 2002). Among the above entities, Beijing Yongxin Spray Cotton Co., Ltd., Beijing Dongcheng District Zhuyuan Food Store, Beijing Ruilongsen Logistics Co., Ltd., and Beijing Fuhaihua Import and Export Co., Ltd. issued "Fund Explanations" for the payments made, all stating that the funds they remitted to Shenghefa Company were used by Song Yu for the purchase of some commercial housing units in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan developed by Shenghefa Company.

Separately, during the retrial hearing of this Court, regarding the fact found by the Beijing High People's Court's retrial that most of the houses involved in the case had new right holders and had been occupied and used, the agent ad litem of Song Yu stated that as for Shenghefa Company's resale of the houses involved in the case, Song Yu initially did not know to whom they were sold. At that time, after the houses involved were delivered to Song Yu, Song Yu did not actually move in. The other party's sales consulted Song Yu, asking whether to sell when the price was high. Song Yu said that if the price was appropriate, they could sell. Song Yu did not know how many were ultimately sold. To date, Shenghefa Company has not returned the proceeds from the sale of the houses to Song Yu. Shenghefa Company stated that most of the houses involved had been sold starting in 2006, that Song Yu had entrusted it to sell them, and it acknowledged the above statement by Song Yu's side regarding the entrustment process. At the same time, Shenghefa Company admitted that it had received the proceeds from the sale but was unclear whether it had given them to Song Yu. The agent ad litem of Song Yu later stated that Shenghefa Company had not told Song Yu whether it had sold the houses.

Further, according to the court's request, after the hearing, Shenghefa Company submitted four other commercial housing sales contract texts signed by Shenghefa Company around the time of Song Yu's house purchase in 2001. The numbers were NO.079876, NO.079878, NO.079877, and NO.079899, with signing dates in October or November 2001. The last page of each of the four contracts bore the "Chao Yang District Housing and Land Administration Bureau Special Seal for Registration of Commercial Housing Pre-sale and Pre-purchase." Based on this, Shenghefa Company argued that the contract numbers of other purchasers were close to or consecutive with the numbers of the contracts involved, indicating they belonged to the same batch, suggesting that the contracts involved were normal.

This Court finds that other facts found upon retrial are consistent with those found by the Beijing High People's Court's retrial.

This Court holds: Considering the petition requests and reasons of the parties, the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether there was a procedural error in the original judgment; 2. Whether the commercial housing sales relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company was genuine and valid.

(1) Regarding whether there was a procedural error in the original judgment.

Article 177, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that if the Supreme People's Court finds a definite error in a legally effective judgment or ruling of a local people's court at any level, or if a higher people's court finds such an error in a judgment or ruling of a lower people's court, it has the authority to bring the case up for trial or to direct a lower people's court to retry it. Therefore, the Beijing High People's Court, pursuant to this provision, initiated a retrial procedure ex officio for the civil judgment of the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court (2006) Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 16218. This was in accordance with the law and procedurally proper. Regarding the issue of the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court allowing Urban and Rural Construction to participate in the retrial as a third party without independent claims, according to Article 56, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, if a third party does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the two parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest for it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings. In this case, the houses involved were already seized in 2004 in the case of Urban and Rural Construction v. Shenghefa Company concerning a dispute over a construction project contract, and were the subject of compulsory enforcement. Moreover, Shenghefa Company's business license has been revoked, and it has essentially no other property available for enforcement. Therefore, the outcome of this case has a legal interest for Urban and Rural Construction. The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court's decision to add Urban and Rural Construction as a third party without independent claims in the retrial was not improper. Song Yu's petition request on this ground lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Regarding whether the commercial housing sales relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company was genuine and valid.

The main evidence Song Yu provided to support the claim that the commercial housing sales contract was genuine and valid includes: 1. Seventeen commercial housing sales contracts. The parties all had no objection to the authenticity of the signatures and seals on the contracts. 2. Ten receipts for house purchase payments, proving that Shenghefa Company acknowledged that Song Yu had paid the full purchase price for the 37 houses (17 purchased in Song Yu's name). 3. An occupancy notice, proving that he had actually taken delivery of the houses involved. These three pieces of evidence all occurred internally between Shenghefa Company and Song Yu. The commercial housing sales contracts were only signed and sealed by the two parties, with no registration or filing with the relevant real estate management authorities. The ten receipts were issued unilaterally by Shenghefa Company, with no formal invoices. The house occupancy notice also bore only the seal of Shenghefa Company.

Based on the facts now established in this case and the statements made by Song Yu and Shenghefa Company in previous proceedings, the following doubts exist regarding the genuineness of the commercial housing sales relationship:

1. This case originated in 2004 when Urban and Rural Construction, due to a dispute over a construction project contract, applied for compulsory enforcement against Shenghefa Company's property (mainly the 17 houses involved and the 10 houses each purchased in the names of Zhang Jingsheng and Guan Hongbiao). Song Yu filed this lawsuit to resist the compulsory enforcement, causing the suspension of the enforcement measures. It was precisely during the period of suspension that Shenghefa Company successively sold most of the remaining houses involved. Regarding the large amount of property he had acquired, Song Yu merely entrusted Shenghefa Company to "sell if the price is appropriate" and showed no concern for the specific timing of sales, the prices, the number of units sold, or the recovery of funds. From October 2006 when Song Yu filed the first-instance lawsuit in the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court until the retrial by this Court, Shenghefa Company, on the one hand, successively sold most of the aforementioned houses separately, and on the other hand, acknowledged Song Yu's claim regarding the purchase of the houses involved. Neither party provided a reasonable explanation for this situation.

2. The commercial housing sales contracts themselves contained doubts. According to the facts found in the original trial, blank contracts numbered 125401 to 125425 were obtained by Beijing Wuyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and blank contracts numbered 130126 to 130150 were obtained by Beijing Wanquan Garden Property Development Co., Ltd. The contracts in dispute, numbered 125415, 125417-125423, 125425, 130131-130135, etc., had already been signed and used by the aforementioned two companies. Shenghefa Company had no reasonable explanation for the source of the contract texts involved. Additionally, the contracts involved were not registered or filed with the real estate management authorities, whereas the four contracts submitted by Shenghefa Company after the hearing of this Court from third-party purchasers all bore the registration and filing seal of the real estate management department.

3. The performance of the contracts involved was highly questionable. Overall, the performance of the contracts was very casual. Regarding the payment situation, a large amount of cash transactions (over 7 million yuan) were involved in the purchase payments, supported only by Song Yu's own statements with no other evidence. Shenghefa Company, on the one hand, claimed that the cash portion was mainly collected by its former legal representative, Wang Yongwei, and on the other hand, acknowledged that Song Yu had paid the full purchase price. As for the transfer portion, the transfer dates from Beijing Dongcheng District Zhuyuan Food Store and Beijing Yongxin Spray Cotton Co., Ltd. to Shenghefa Company were both April 30, 2001. During the original trial of this case, they issued "Fund Explanations" stating that the payments were used by Song Yu to purchase some commercial housing units in Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan developed by Shenghefa Company. However, according to Song Yu's statement, the relationship between him and Shenghefa Company in April 2001 was one of borrowing, and it was only after June 2001 that the loan was converted into a house purchase payment, creating an obvious contradiction. Regarding the payment vouchers, Song Yu only submitted ten receipts issued by Shenghefa Company, with no formal invoices. During the retrial by the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, Song Yu explained this by saying, "I never had invoices issued for the houses I bought. I didn't even think about getting invoices." This explanation is unconvincing. Formally, the numbering of the ten receipts was reversed in relation to the issuance time, and the amounts on the receipts did not correspond one-to-one with each specific payment. Regarding the occupancy situation, the Shenghe Jiayuan project passed the completion acceptance inspection on April 26, 2002, and occupancy procedures began in May of the same year. Song Yu had already signed the purchase contract in 2001 and paid the full purchase price by April 28, 2002, but Shenghefa Company only issued a house occupancy notice to him in May 2003. Although Song Yu claimed to have completed occupancy procedures, he did not sign a property management service contract with the property management company and did not actually move in.

4. Yuecai Company registered a mortgage on the houses involved in July 2001 and September 2003. When signing the mortgage contracts, Shenghefa Company did not inform Yuecai Company that the houses involved had been sold. The occupancy notice issued by Shenghefa Company to Song Yu was dated May 28, 2003, and Song Yu also claimed to have completed occupancy procedures on that day. However, the second mortgage registration on the houses involved was on September 15, 2003, and Song Yu raised no objection at that time. As a buyer who paid the full price, Song Yu also did not file an appeal when the first-instance judgment ranked his rights behind the bank's later mortgage rights.

5. In the "Shenghe Jiayuan Project Fund Source Detail Table" (as of October 10, 2001), one column recorded: Unit: Song Yu; Nature: Loan; Amount: RMB 11 million. Also listed was pre-collected sales revenue of RMB 114.41 million. According to the claims of Shenghefa Company and Song Yu, by October 2001, the RMB 11 million loan had been converted into a house purchase payment, but the table still listed Song Yu's RMB 11 million loan alongside the sales revenue. Meanwhile, in the concurrent "Shenghe Jiayuan Project Fund Flow Detail Table" (as of October 10, 2001), one column recorded: Repayment of Song Yu loan RMB 11 million. Now Song Yu and Shenghefa Company both claim the RMB 11 million loan had been converted into a house purchase payment, but they failed to provide a reasonable explanation for the repayment recorded in the above table. Moreover, for such a large amount of fund flow and a large number of house transactions, the parties relied only on oral statements and failed to provide any written agreement on the conversion of the loan into a house purchase payment. Regarding how the loan was converted into a house purchase payment and the process of the house purchase, Song Yu's statements varied on multiple occasions, were contradictory, and he was unable to provide other evidence.

6. On April 29, 2002, Urban and Rural Construction and Shenghefa Company signed a key transfer letter, which stated that the project involved had passed the acceptance inspection on April 24, 2002, and Urban and Rural Construction transferred five keys per unit of the already pre-sold houses to Shenghefa Company. On May 22, 2002, Urban and Rural Construction and Shenghefa Company signed an IOU, stating that to facilitate Shenghefa Company's subsequent house sales needs, Urban and Rural Construction lent Shenghefa Company the keys (one key per unit) for the unsold units in Buildings 1 and 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan. The attached sales list for Building 2 of Shenghe Jiayuan showed the houses involved as unsold. The main purpose of signing the above documents was to facilitate the house transfer and to support Shenghefa Company's subsequent sales activities; there was no reason to conceal the sale to Song Yu at that time.

This Court holds: The key issue in this case is whether the commercial housing sales relationship truly existed. The sales relationship in this case is clearly inconsistent with normal transactions of the same type. Although both Shenghefa Company and Song Yu claimed in the proceedings that a genuine and valid commercial housing sales relationship existed between them, Song Yu's statements on important facts such as signing the purchase contract and paying the purchase price varied on multiple occasions and were contradictory. Given the numerous doubts outlined above, the basis for finding a genuine commercial housing sales relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company is clearly insufficient. The original judgment's finding that no genuine commercial housing sales relationship existed between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company was not improper, and this Court affirms it.

Song Yu claimed that the RMB 10.5 million remitted by Shenghefa Company via check to Huanan Industrial Account on July 25, 2001, did not match the loan amount in the loan contract between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company, and the original judgment did not clarify this. Moreover, the original judgment could not explain the over RMB 8 million Song Yu paid to Shenghefa Company in 2002. This Court holds: This judgment only denies the genuineness of the house sales relationship between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company. The flow of funds between Song Yu and Shenghefa Company constitutes a separate legal relationship and is not within the scope of this case.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 186, paragraph 1 and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is rendered as follows:

Affirm the civil judgment of the Beijing High People's Court (2010) Gao Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 1715.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Xin Zhengyu

Acting Judge: Wang Dan

Acting Judge: Si Wei

Clerk: Wei Da
